chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who sells an item, so the buyer says, 'It is for such and such,' being less than what the seller said. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The word is the word of the seller along with his oath, when the item remains standing in its essence.'

key_terms.قَائِماً بِعَيْنِهِ: standing in its essence / remaining as is

ai.seo_question: Who has the final say in a sale if the buyer and seller disagree on the price?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of *qawl al-ba'i* (the seller's testimony) in cases of price discrepancy, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the seller is the primary possessor of the item and thus has the stronger claim to its value. The condition that the item remains 'in its original state' (*qayiman bi-'aynihi*) ensures that the ruling applies specifically to undamaged goods where the seller's knowledge of the initial asking price is most reliable. This ruling underscores the importance of oaths (*yamin*) in commercial disputes within Shia fiqh to resolve ambiguity in favor of the party holding the asset.
